title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 27 (Agreement in restraint of trade, void)

content.overview: Section 27 provides that every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void. Exception 1: One who sells the goodwill of a business may agree with the buyer to refrain from carrying on a similar business, within specified local limits, so long as the buyer, or any person deriving title to the goodwill from him, carries on a like business therein, provided that such limits appear to the Court reasonable, regard being had to the nature of the business.
content.glance: Restraint of lawful profession/trade/business → void to that extent; exception for reasonable local restraint on sale of goodwill.
content.study: Every agreement restraining anyone from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business is to that extent void. Exception 1 allows a seller of goodwill to agree not to carry on a similar business within specified local limits that appear reasonable to the Court, while the buyer (or successor) carries on a like business there. Current-law framing: identify the restraint; apply voidness to that extent; test Exception 1 (goodwill, local limits, reasonableness).

sections.heading: General rule
sections.body: Agreement restraining exercise of a lawful profession, trade or business is to that extent void.

sections.heading: Exception — sale of goodwill
sections.body: Seller of goodwill may agree to refrain from similar business within specified local limits that appear reasonable, while buyer carries on like business therein.

provisions.title: Agreement in restraint of trade, void

examples.title: Sale of goodwill
examples.body: A sells the goodwill of a business to B and agrees not to carry on a similar business within reasonable local limits while B carries on the business. Exception 1 may save the restraint.

hypotheticals.question: Are all non-compete clauses void in India?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 27 voids restraints on lawful profession, trade or business to that extent, subject to Exception 1 (and other recognised exceptions such as those under partnership law where applicable).

misconceptions.trap: Reasonable restraints of trade are generally valid as in English common law.
misconceptions.correction: Section 27 is stricter: every such restraint is void to that extent, with a limited statutory exception for sale of goodwill.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 27 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the restraint on profession/trade/business. II. Apply voidness to that extent. III. Test Exception 1. IV. Conclude.

examTips: State the general rule and Exception 1.
